scenes.narration: The genes do not care about Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo; they care about copies. Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo (Korean: 달의 연인 – 보보경심 려) is a South Korean television series based on the Chinese novel Bu Bu Jing Xin by Tong Hua. It aired from August 29 to November 1, 2016, on SBS, every Monday and Tuesday at 22:00 (KST), for 20 episodes.

Take away the meaning and Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo still functions — that is the disturbing part. It recorded an average nationwide viewership rating of 7.6% per Nielsen Korea and 7.3% per TNMS, and was considered a failure against its US$13 million production budget. During a total solar eclipse, a 25-year-old 21st-century woman, Go Ha-jin (Lee Ji-eun), is transported back in time, to the Goryeo period.

The unconscious does not argue with Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo; it simply acts first. She wakes up in the year of 941, in the body of Hae Soo, among the many princes of the ruling Wang family, during the reign of King Taejo. She initially falls in love with the gentle and warm-hearted 8th Prince Wang Wook (Kang Ha-neul), but later develops a relationship with Wang So (Lee Joon-gi), the fearsome 4th Prince, who hides his face behind a mask and is given the derogatory label of "wolf-dog".

Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. As the story develops, Hae Soo finds herself unwittingly caught up in the palace politics and the rivalry among the princes, as they fight for the throne. Initially known as the cruel and aloof one among the princes, he is both feared and misunderstood by those around him.

The bleak reading of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo is also the most testable one. He begins to change because of Hae Soo, who quickly realizes that his coldness is a front to hide his pain. However, his position places him as a rival to Wang So for both love and the throne.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo. A mischievous and playful royal with a lively but annoyingly childish personality who becomes Hae Soo's first friend in Goryeo. One of Hae Soo's friends and a romantic playboy is known for his refined and aristocratic manners.

The self that experiences Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo is a committee, not a king. The youngest Prince who has a crush on Hae Soo and befriends her, also stays by her side until she dies. As per her last wish, Wang Jung then raises Hae Soo and Wang So's daughter.

Reproduction explains more of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo than any philosophy dares to admit. On June 25, 2015, director Kim Kyu-tae and his production company, BaramiBunda Inc., announced that they were in the early stages of making a Korean version of the Chinese novel Bu Bu Jing Xin by Tong Hua. YG Entertainment and NBC Universal invested in the series, with the latter covering half of the budget of ₩15 billion.

Once you see Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. The Chinese streaming platform Youku bought Moon Lovers at $400,000 per episode, making it the most expensive Korean drama ever sold, surpassing the records previously set by Descendants of the Sun (2016) and Uncontrollably Fond (2016), which were sold to China for $250,000 per episode. The record was beaten a few months later by Man to Man (2017).

The story Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. On November 11, 2015 it was announced that Lee Joon-gi had been offered the male lead part of Wang So. The actor confirmed his participation in the project on January 4, 2016, and the same day it was announced that singer-actress Lee Ji-eun had accepted the part of the female lead.

Meaning is not found in Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo — it is manufactured for it. The jewels in the drama were all created by Jung Jae-in of Minhwi Art Jewelry, and Lee Ji-eun herself designed the hairpin with the peony gifted by Wang So to the female lead. Artist Lee Hoo-chang designed and supervised the production of the over one hundred masks for the drama.

The cold light on Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Filming, which lasted five months, began in February 2016 at the Yoseonjeong pavilion and the Yoseon-am rocks in Yeongwol County, Gangwon Province, ending in the early hours of July 1, when Lee Ji-eun filmed her last scene from episode 20. Lee Joon-gi ended his part on June 30 on the set in Icheon, Gyeonggi Province.

Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. On August 27, 2016, two days before the airing of the series, South Korean channel SBS aired a one-hour preview containing a historical introduction presented by History professor Seol Min-seok, behind the scenes and interviews with the actors. A second special episode, containing the historical introduction already presented in the August preview and a summary of the first seven episodes, was broadcast on September 14, for the Chuseok.

The honest version of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo starts by giving up the comforting part. The 20-episode drama officially started from August 29 on Mondays and Tuesdays, simultaneously in China, Hong Kong, Australia, Cambodia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and Indonesia, airing the first two episodes back to back, and ended on November 1, 2016. On September 3, SBS aired the first three episodes again in the Director's Cut version following the audience's observations on the soundtrack and the presence of too many characters which were considered a source of distraction.

Strip Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. After the premiere, audience reviews were mixed, with the adaptation, the soundtrack, the photography, and Lee Joon-gi's acting being praised, while Byun Baek-hyun's performances received criticism. Lee Ji-eun's performance received mixed reviews: some critics believed the actress was doing a good job despite the frequent mood changes from one scene to the other, while others believed that director Kim Kyu-tae's trademark close-ups revealed her lack of emotion.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo shows exactly where that breaks. According to Lee Woong of Yonhap News, the first part of the drama, which highlighted the love triangle and had almost all conflicts stemming from Queen Yoo's pathological love for Wang Yo, made the entire series too fragile. There were also doubts about the plausibility of the developments, such as the historical knowledge of the female lead, and that Wang So's scar could be covered with makeup.

What looks like free choice in Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo is older than choice itself. The opinions on the finale were discordant: despite the good acting performances of the actors, viewers complained about the excessive product placement in the last episode. Park Si-eun's and Woo Hee-jin's acting in their last episodes was also praised for its solidity and maturity.

Nobody designed the part of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo you experience — it was inherited. The reception abroad and on the Internet was more positive than in South Korea. On Youku, it reached 300 million views after the first three episodes, more than a billion views after episode 9, and two billions after episode 18.

Every serious account of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. It topped Taiwan's VOD service website KKTV Drama Chart in the September 19–25 week, and was the top content on Hong Kong VOD service's Laiko since the first week of September. On DramaFever, which made it available in North and South America, it recorded more than two million views mid-airing of the series.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. According to Nielsen Korea, the first episode recorded a nationwide viewership rating of 7.4%, then taking a downward trend. Ratings started rising in the second half of the series, and reached the highest rating with the last episode, which recorded the 11.3%.

The selfish-gene reading of Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo makes it less romantic and far more precise. With an average nationwide rating of 7.6% for Nielsen Korea and 7.3% for TNMS, the drama was considered a failure for performing below expectations. The main cause was identified in the decision to film the whole series before airing, which made it impossible to make changes on the way based on feedback.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. SBS tried to remedy by re-editing the episodes aired domestically starting with the sixth. The fact that the drama wasn't an original story, but a remake, was also indicated as a reason for the disappointing ratings because it created in the potential audience the preconceived idea that the story was heavy and difficult to approach.

The feeling that Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. For Hankook Ilbo, the audience was tired of bad guys and complicated emotions, preferring instead a kind male lead and a simple story like in Love in the Moonlight, which aired simultaneously on KBS2. With the end of Love in the Moonlight on October 18, viewership rating started increasing steadily and Moon Lovers was the most watched drama on the evening of October 24.

Nothing in Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo was chosen as the most anticipated series of the second half of 2016 in China. The previews released through Naver TV cast reached more than one million views each in early October.

The psychology underneath Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo is simpler and older than the story on top. In Singapore it was number three in 2016 Google Trends (TV shows section). According to the research institute Good Data Corporation, the series was the third most discussed drama of 2016, after KBS dramas Descendants of the Sun and Love in the Moonlight.
